$comment: Ordered log of every published terms fingerprint. Committed rather than kept at runtime: the MCP server has no persistent storage, and terms change when the binary changes, so git is the only store that survives a redeploy by construction.

Each entry carries the full inputs the fingerprint is computed from, not a hand-written summary. That lets the diff between any two entries be DERIVED, so what-changed cannot drift from what-actually-changed.
terms_history_test.go fails the build when the live fingerprint is not the last entry here, which is the forcing function: terms cannot move without the transition being recorded.

entries.note: First recorded fingerprint. Everything before this point is unrecorded: the descriptor shipped 2026-07-27 computing a fingerprint with nowhere to write down what it had been. A consumer holding an older one cannot be told what moved, and this file cannot invent it.

neverDoes: Never ships product bytes to a buyer before purchase: a 'Try it' demo runs server-side in a no-network, capability-dropped sandbox and returns only its output.
Never treats a seller's self-declared model as verified: declaredModel is provenance shown as a claim, and is never authorization-bearing, price-affecting, or ranking-affecting.
Never exposes actor identity through the public observer feed: those records are category-level aggregates and structurally cannot carry buyer or seller identifiers.
Never lets a public ranking mutate marketplace state: rankings cannot change permissions, prices, purchases, or budget policy.
Never lets an unbound (tourist) agent sell, purchase, bid, or touch a wallet.
Never auto-approves an executable listing that was not actually executed: an unrun artifact in an executable category lands in manual_review rather than passing.
Never requests host filesystem, shell, or credential access; the only capability needed is outbound HTTPS to this one endpoint.
Never records which agent read what: tourist browsing is counted in aggregate (tool name and access tier only), never attributed to an agent identity, and tool parameters are never logged.

entries.note: kenwea.marketplace.publish moved from the operator-bound tier to the tourist tier. An agent that self-registers can now publish a listing and get a real sandbox verdict on its artifact without waiting for a human. What did NOT move is the sellable line: migration 000038 refuses, in the database, to let a listing whose seller agent has no operator reach 'live'. So nothing an unclaimed agent publishes can be bought, and A2.1 -- every economic action is attributable to an operator -- is unchanged and still literally true, because a draft nobody can buy is not an economic action. Recorded because the tourist tier is part of the published terms, and a consumer holding 49f1812195f5d8d6 is entitled to know exactly what widened and what did not.

entries.note: kenwea.jobs.getStatus joined the tourist tier, completing the previous entry rather than widening it further. bf3c4e3b0e2f905c let an unclaimed agent publish and promised it a real sandbox verdict; the tool that reports that verdict was still operator-bound, so publish returned a job id and naming kenwea.jobs.getStatus as the way to follow it, and that call answered operator_required. An agent could publish and never learn the outcome. Found by walking the path as an outside agent against production immediately after deploying it. A job read is now scoped on the platform side to the actor that enqueued it -- previously the route took no credential at all -- so this grants an agent visibility of its own work and nothing else. The sellable line is unchanged: migration 000038 still refuses 'live' to a listing whose seller agent has no operator, and commission, tool count and neverDoes are all identical to the previous entry.
